about: Settings schema v2 (spec section 3): the 20 keys of inputs/spike-matchdg/extraction/schema.md (since 1) plus 5 data-pipeline keys (since 2). Version-1 values are free-form, per method as {method: value}; version-2 values are lists of entries with enumerated fields, so a fixed script can compare them. The extractor prompts and both answer schemas are built from this file.

keys.describe: the domains the model trains on
the domains the reported numbers are evaluated on

keys.describe_paper: the domains the paper states are used
keys.describe_code: the domains for which data actually exists in the repository or is produced by its scripts

keys.describe: training examples per domain
validation examples per domain
parameters of the data generation (synthetic data, subsets)
the model
the optimizer
0.0 means plain SGD with no momentum; null means the source does not say
Nesterov momentum
the learning rate
how the learning rate changes over training
weight decay
batch size
number of training epochs
how the reported epoch or checkpoint is chosen
one entry per term in the training objective (e.g. cross-entropy, a penalty), with its weight and how the weight changes over training
number of runs (seeds) behind each reported number
what the reported numbers measure
how the reported numbers aggregate the runs, including what the printed spread is (standard deviation or standard error); give it per reported quantity as {"<quantity>": value} where it differs
resizing of the inputs before they reach the model
normalization of the inputs (e.g. subtracting a mean and dividing by a standard deviation)

random transforms applied to the data, on the fly or as a stored augmented copy: what they are (snake_case names, in the order applied), whether they come before or after the transform that makes each domain, and every split and use that reads the augmented data (training, validation, model selection, evaluation), per method and training phase

how each domain is made from the base data, including the direction (sign) of a rotation. `kind` names the mechanism, not what the source calls it: rotation = inputs rotated by a per-domain angle; other_geometric = translation, scaling, shear; photometric = colour, brightness, contrast, texture or style; feature_noise = a per-domain fraction or level of an input feature is replaced or perturbed by noise; label_noise = a per-domain fraction of labels is corrupted; correlation_strength = examples are sampled so that an attribute co-occurs with the label at a per-domain rate; source_dataset = each domain is a different dataset, site or collection. Describe the details in `params`

the data each selection step reads: the choice of the reported epoch or checkpoint (use checkpoint) and the choice of hyperparameters (use hyperparameter_tuning): which split, of which domains, and which version of it (plain or augmented), per method and training phase
